title: Extraction of High Molecular Weight DNA from Aphids for Long-Read Sequencing
author: Roland Wouters
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhftj3nn
materials: (Optional) repeat the wash step 2 more times.

Assess the quality of DNA by electrophoresis and spectrophotometry. A single, high-molecular-weight band should be visible, a smear at lower molecular weight indicates fragmentation and/or RNA contamination. Absorbance ratio of 260:280 and 260:230 should both be 1.8 or greater. If you suspended the pellet in TE, ensure than you blank the spectrophotometer with TE. Determine the concentration of the DNA using a fluorescent dye-binding based method such as the Qubit (Invitrogen).

steps.title: Grind frozen aphids
steps.instruction: Place approximately 10 mg (≈20 frozen aphids from a single female) in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube with a plastic pestle pre‑cooled in liquid nitrogen; keep tissue frozen and crush by an up‑down motion without turning the pestle.

steps.title: Add reagent 1 and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 600 µl of reagent 1 (containing RNase) while leaving the pestle in the tube, agitate the pestle to mix thoroughly, then remove the pestle keeping as much material as possible; incubate at 37 °C for 30 min with occasional inversion mixing.

steps.title: Add reagent 2
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl of reagent 2 and mix by inversion until a uniform solution is obtained.

steps.title: Optional proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: If desired, add 10 µl proteinase K (600 U ml⁻¹) and incubate at 55 °C for 2 h with occasional inversion mixing; if proteinase K is omitted, incubate at 65 °C for 10 min with regular inversion mixing.

steps.title: Ice incubation
steps.instruction: Place the samples on ice for 20 min.

steps.title: Add chloroform and resin
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl pre‑cooled chloroform (‑20 °C) and 100 µl Nucleon PhytoPure DNA extraction resin suspension, mix gently by shaking and inversion, then rotate on a rotator disk for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Phase separation by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1 300 g for 10 min; carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new tube without disturbing the interface, leaving a small amount behind to avoid chloroform or resin carry‑over.

steps.title: Optional sodium acetate addition
steps.instruction: Add 0.05 × volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) to the transferred aqueous phase, if desired.

steps.title: Isopropanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (1 ×) of pre‑cooled isopropanol (‑20 °C) one drop at a time, invert to mix, then incubate at ‑20 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4 000 g for 10 min, discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, and place the tube top‑down on a paper roll to dry further.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 1 ml freshly prepared 70 % ethanol, invert the tube five times, then centrifuge at 4 000 g for 20 min to re‑pellet the DNA.

steps.title: Final ethanol removal and drying
steps.instruction: Pour off the ethanol without disturbing the pellet and dry the sample by placing the tube top‑down on a paper roll.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 100 µl of water or TE buffer.

steps.title: Assess DNA size
steps.instruction: Evaluate the molecular weight of the DNA by running the sample on an Agilent FEMTO‑pulse Fragment Analyzer or by pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis (PFGE).
